note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Question a, wording: The options say 'at a large angle' and 'at a small angle' without saying the angle is the angle of incidence, measured from the normal. In everyday speech, light hitting a surface 'at a small angle' means a grazing ray, which would make the second option right. Say 'large angle of incidence (measured from the normal)' or 'beyond the critical angle'.

rejected.title: Total internal reflection and optical fibres
card: When light goes from a material with a higher refractive index to one with a lower index, such as glass to air, it bends away from the normal.
The critical angle is the angle of incidence at which the refracted ray runs along the boundary. Beyond it, no light escapes and all of it reflects back inside.
Total internal reflection needs two things: light travelling in the higher index material, and an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle.

An optical fibre is a thin glass core with a lower index coating around it. Light signals hit the wall beyond the critical angle, so they reflect again and again along the fibre with very little loss.
rejected.remember: Beyond the critical angle, light inside the higher index material reflects completely, so fibres can guide it.

a.q: Which situation can produce total internal reflection?
opts: Light in glass hitting a glass-air boundary at a large angle
Light in air hitting a glass boundary at a large angle
Light in glass hitting a glass-air boundary at a small angle
Light in air hitting a water boundary at a small angle
a.why: Total internal reflection needs light in the higher index material and an angle beyond the critical angle. Air to glass fails the first need. A small angle in glass fails the second.
a.clue: Check both conditions: which material, and which angle.

b.q: Why does a light signal stay inside an optical fibre instead of leaking out through the side?
opts: It hits the wall beyond the critical angle and reflects
It hits the wall below the critical angle and is absorbed
The coating has a higher index than the core and traps it
The signal is a sound wave that cannot leave the glass
b.why: The core has a higher index than the coating, and the light meets the wall beyond the critical angle, so all of it reflects. A higher index coating would let light escape instead.
b.clue: Think about the angle at the wall of the core.
